signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme
signals.text: The G10 scorecard reveals severe bilateral divergence: JPY averages +1.310% across 7 pairs while SEK drops −0.751% across 2 pairs, generating an outsized 2.061% spread. Revised Japan Q2 GDP printed at 1.4% annualized against 1.1% expected, reinforcing BoJ hike expectations heading into the 18 September meeting. This macro push contrasts directly with SEK, burdened by an ESI of −26.7 showing persistent economic data misses. Despite JPY carrying a nominal deficit against SEK (BoJ 1.0% vs SEK 1.75% — 75bp spread favoring SEK), policy repricing and GDP outperformance dominate cross-asset flows. Trade bias: Long JPY/SEK; widening G10 performance spread favors continued bilateral trend. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: BoJ leaves policy guidance dovish, causing an abrupt unwind of the 2.061% spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.76, holding beneath its daily SMA20 (158.72), SMA50 (160.33), and SMA200 (158.44). CFTC positioning shows JPY Leveraged Funds net short at −111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z −2.18), reflecting crowded short exposure vulnerable to aggressive covering. Options pricing heavily reinforces downside risk: 25d risk reversals print at −2.55 (Saxo, 1M tenor, indicative mid), displaying extreme put skew despite ATM IV running at 7.2% against HV30 of 11.5% (VRP −4.3%). Although Fed SOFR at 3.66% vs BoJ TONA at 0.98% maintains a +268bp carry advantage for the dollar, spec squeeze risk and downside option hedging dominate spot price action. Trade bias: Short USD/JPY; technical breakdown below the SMA cluster targets deeper mean reversion. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Strong US inflation data on Friday halts the liquidation and revives the carry trade.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Spec Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7214, sitting comfortably above its daily SMA20 at 0.7144 and SMA50 at 0.7048. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds stretched long at +50,250 contracts, ranking at the 94th percentile (z +1.79) of its 52-week range. However, WoW net positioning declined by 3,328 contracts while spot pushed higher, pointing to late-trend momentum exhaustion. This institutional crowding contrasts with Myfxbook retail sentiment at 90% short, presenting an extreme contrarian retail divergence. With RBA AONIA at 4.35% vs Fed SOFR at 3.66% providing a 69bp carry cushion, spot remains supported but vulnerable to institutional long profit-taking. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional trend remains intact but upside is constrained by crowded positioning. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Broad USD rally on upcoming US CPI triggers Leveraged Fund liquidation below 0.7144.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Yield Drag
signals.text: GBP/USD prints at 1.3538, pressing just below its daily SMA20 at 1.3556 while remaining above the SMA50/200 base at 1.3461/1.3449. Options implied volatility on GBP/USD trades at 11.0% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.5%, producing an outsized +6.5% Vol Risk Premium (CBOE BPVIX). This pronounced vol premium highlights heavy institutional hedging demand into upcoming UK parliamentary hearings and BoE decisions. Furthermore, the UK real policy rate sits at +0.35% (BoE 3.75% minus 3.40% inflation expectations), lagging the US real rate of +1.38% and narrowing structural support. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; heavy options hedging and real rate differentials cap immediate breakout momentum. Catalyst: UK Monetary Policy Report Hearings today at 13:15 UTC. Risk: A clean break and daily close above 1.3556 invalidates the cap and retests recent highs.
evidence: GBP real rate: +0.35% vs USD real rate: +1.38%
